speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment in light of heat wave conditions in neighbouring countries such as Malaysia and Thailand (a) what is the Ministry's assessment of the risk of similar heat wave events affecting Singapore; and (b) whether there are plans to enhance advance warning systems for weather-dependent sectors.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: So, in view of this developments, may I ask the Senior Minister of State: one, given that Singapore's current approach is based on a heat stress advisory, whether the Ministry considers this sufficiently robust and actionable, or if there are plans to introduce a more formalised alert system, with clear thresholds and corresponding response measures?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Are there also plans to increase the number of sensors that we put around various parts of Singapore?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My second question relates to Singapore being a highly urbanised city-state.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: And lastly, on worker protection, can the Senior Minister of State clarify whether existing heat stress guidelines for employers remain adequate in the event of a more prolonged or intense heat conditions?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Because I note that current heat stress measures are focused more on outdoor workers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Will the Government consider extending more formal protections or guidance to other at-risk sectors, such as indoor, non-air-conditioned workplaces, because most of our factories are non-air-conditioned, as well as for delivery riders who spend a lot of time outdoors?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: He first asked about the advisory and whether it needed to be more formal, and whether it was robust and actionable.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I would characterise our position thus: and I would say it is robust, it is formalised, it is actionable.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The heat advisory that goes out is clearly defined.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In my original answer, I explained what a heat wave was.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are clear definitions that we have been using in Singapore since 2016, if I recall.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so, it is objective, it is measurable, it is specific.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And then, agencies – he cited the example of MOM looking at outdoor workers – have developed action plans.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These then are triggered by the information that is provided by the MSS.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, MSS, the National Environmental Agency, has a certain set of definitions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: When the thresholds are reached, advisories are issued that fall into certain pre-specified categories.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And then, various agencies and regulatory bodies will activate their action plan.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, the formalised, robust, actionable processes are already there.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Of course, as related to his later questions, these can and will be improved.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And I will speak about that in a minute.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Member can file a separate Parliamentary Question (PQ), a written PQ perhaps, about the specific number.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Historically, not all of them were used for heat reporting, but today, all of them are, for air temperature.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And then, we have, if I recall, another 27 Wet-Bulb Globe Temperature stations across Singapore.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, our overall coverage for sensors is pretty good.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, the short answer to the second half of his first supplementary question is about the sense-making, as well as his other two questions – this is work that the Heat Resilience Policy Office will indeed be taking up.
